context: Filed 2026-11-20 from the adversarial review of the scale-factor and TPC-DI remediation work (PRs #4298-#4385 and benchbox-site #178-#210).
description:
## Problem
18 TPC-DI sidecars carry this token for old-generator reasons: 12 from #4307 and 6 from #4222 ('Generated before the TPC-DI scale correction'); 3 more from #3645 have no custom reason and are out of scope. #4307 flagged 12 TPC-DI bundles produced by an older generator with `defective-variant-or-loader-wrong-result`, whose canonical text says the run produced wrong values. They are only from an older generator; a custom `known_defect_reason` overrides the displayed text.

## Change
Propose a label id and text for 'produced by a superseded data generator; not comparable with current bundles', then relabel the 12 sidecars.

## Decision gates
The owner approves the label id and text before anything is committed: defect labels are public corpus taxonomy and appear in the Explorer. Check how the site renders an unknown label before proposing an id.

## Verification rubric
Pass: the 12 sidecars carry the approved label; bundle bytes and hashes are unchanged; corpus validation and the inventory check pass; ranking exclusion of the 12 is unchanged.

## Additions from the item review
- The owner decides whether #4222's six are relabelled with #4307's twelve.
- This touches the same `KNOWN_DEFECT_TOKENS` and reasons hunk in benchbox/validation/bundle.py as #4340's new label: start after #4340 merges, or put both labels to the owner as one question.
- Rubric addition: the deployed Explorer renders the approved label.

## Guardrails
- Any limit, default, threshold or label id or text is shown to the owner before it is committed. Briefs quote owner answers verbatim; questions to the owner carry no preselected answer.
- The implementer replies on review threads and leaves resolving them to the reviewer or the owner, unless the owner says otherwise (AGENTS.md asks agents to resolve benchbox-oracle threads on soundness paths; the owner has been asked which applies).
- Hosted writes (merge, close, disable or enable auto-merge, workflow dispatch, remote branch delete) only as the repository's close-out procedure or the owner's word for that pull request allows; never raw `gh pr merge` in core.
- No polling loop around `make pr-arm`, no `--no-verify`, no stand-in review unless the owner names the PR and head unprompted. Push only after `make pr-preflight` exits 0 on the exact head.
- No worktree takeover while another session may be working; no tracker write from a server that reports a stale version; never chain `git stash` with `git stash pop`.
- Heavy work runs only through `make heavy-run` or a lock-taking entry point, one run at a time.
- Status reports state only what merged and what was verified, with the evidence.
